arxiv-2012-14266.title: A search for hard X-ray bursts occurring simultaneously to fast radio bursts in the repeating FRB 121102
arxiv-2012-14266.creator: Shangyu Sun, Wenfei Yu, Yunwei Yu, Dongming Mao
arxiv-2012-14266.description: Abstract The nature of fast radio bursts (FRBs) is currently unknown. Repeating FRBs offer better opportunity than non-repeating FRBs since their simultaneous multi-wavelength counterparts might be identified. The magnetar flare model of FRBs is one of the most promising models which predicts high energy emission in addition to radio burst emission.

arxiv-2106-01055.title: A Novel Edge Detection Operator for Identifying Buildings in Augmented Reality Applications
arxiv-2106-01055.creator: Ciprian Orhei, Silviu Vert, Radu Vasiu
arxiv-2106-01055.description: Abstract Augmented Reality is an environment-enhancing technology, widely applied in many domains, such as tourism and culture. One of the major challenges in this field is precise detection and extraction of building information through Computer Vision techniques. Edge detection is one of the building blocks operations for many feature extraction solutions in Computer Vision.

arxiv-2111-13719.title: Probing many-body localization by excited-state VQE
arxiv-2111-13719.creator: Shuo Liu, Shi-Xin Zhang, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Shengyu Zhang, Hong Yao
arxiv-2111-13719.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shuo Liu, Shi-Xin Zhang, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Shengyu Zhang, Hong Yao. Non-equilibrium physics including many-body localization (MBL) has attracted increasing attentions, but theoretical approaches of reliably studying non-equilibrium properties remain quite limited. In this Letter, we propose a systematic approach to probe MBL phases via the excited-state variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and demonstrate convincing results of MBL on a quantum hardware, which we believe paves a promising way for future simulations of non-equilibrium systems beyond the reach of classical computations in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum

arxiv-2212-02890.title: Dilution of chemical enrichment in galaxies 600 Myr after the Big Bang
arxiv-2212-02890.creator: Kasper E. Heintz, Gabriel B. Brammer, Clara Giménez-Arteaga, Victoria B. Strait, Claudia del P. Lagos, Aswin P. Vijayan, Jorryt Matthee, Darach Watson, Charlotte A. Mason, Anne Hutter, Sune Toft, Johan P. U. Fynbo, Pascal A. Oesch
arxiv-2212-02890.description: Abstract Galaxies throughout the last 12 Gyr of cosmic time follow a single, universal relation that connects their star-formation rates (SFRs), stellar masses ( M ⋆ M_{\star} ) and chemical abundances Mannucci10 ; Curti20 . Deviation from these fundamental scaling relations would imply a drastic change in the processes that regulate galaxy evolution.

pmc-10643579.title: HMGB2 upregulation promotes the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma cells through the activation of ZEB1/vimentin axis
pmc-10643579.creator: Kai Lu, Teng Zhao, Lixue Yang, Yang Liu, Xiang Ruan, Longjiu Cui, Yongjie Zhang
pmc-10643579.description: BackgroundHigh mobility group box 2 (HMGB2) is abnormally expressed in human cancers and participated in multiple biological behaviors, such as proliferation, invasion and prognosis. However, its role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is largely unknown.MethodsIn clinical sample analysis, 62 HCC patients were enrolled in this study.

pmc-11321861.title: Tape-assisted fabrication method for constructing PDMS membrane-containing culture devices with cyclic radial stretching stimulation
pmc-11321861.creator: Yun-Chen Wu, Jing-Yi Yang, Chia-Hsien Hsu
pmc-11321861.description: Advanced in vitro culture systems have emerged as alternatives to animal testing and traditional cell culture methods in biomedical research. Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) is frequently used in creating sophisticated culture devices owing to its elastomeric properties, which allow mechanical stretching to simulate physiological movements in cell experiments.

pmc-11574850.title: Simple Parameters and Data Processing for Better Signal-to-Noise and Temporal Resolution in In Situ 1D NMR Reaction Monitoring
pmc-11574850.creator: Annabel Flook, Guy C Lloyd-Jones
pmc-11574850.description: In situ 1D NMR spectroscopic reaction monitoring allows detailed investigation of chemical kinetics and mechanism. Concentration versus time data are derived from a time series of NMR spectra. Each spectrum in the series is obtained by Fourier transform of the corresponding FID. When the spectrometer outputs FIDs recorded from multiple scans, the spectra benefit from an increase in signal-to-noise (S/N).

pmc-11655959.title: cfDNA fragmentation patterns correlate with tumor burden measured via PSMA PET/CT volumetric parameters in patients with biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer
pmc-11655959.creator: Gary Amseian, Marcel Figueras, Joel Mases, Lourdes Mengual, Maria-Jose Ribal, Katherine Quintero, Rita Pages, Mercedes Ingelmo-Torres, Fiorella-Lizzeth Roldan, Rocío Caratini, David Fuster, Antonio Alcaraz, Laura Izquierdo, Pilar Paredes, Francisco Campos, Francisco Campos, Sebastián Casanueva-Elice
pmc-11655959.description: BackgroundProstate cancer recurrence following primary treatment poses a significant clinical challenge, particularly when detected through biochemical recurrence at low PSA levels. Conventional imaging modalities often fail to localize the disease at this early stage. PSMA PET has demonstrated superior sensitivity in detecting recurrent lesions, even in patients with low PSA.

pmc-11675654.title: Plant-Based Sunscreen Emulgel: UV Boosting Effect of Bilberry and Green Tea NaDES Extracts
pmc-11675654.creator: Milica Martinović, Ivana Nešić, Dragica Bojović, Ana Žugić, Slavica Blagojević, Stevan Blagojević, Vanja M Tadić, Alexey Vertegel, Luis Morales-Quintana
pmc-11675654.description: Natural deep eutectic solvents (NaDES) were employed for the extraction of bilberry and green tea leaves. This study explored the incorporation of these NaDES extracts into various carrier systems: hydrogels, emulsions, and emulgels stabilized with hydroxyethyl cellulose or xanthan gum.

pmc-11707685.title: Maximal mouth opening is a simple method to evaluate the treatment outcome of temporomandibular joint arthritis in patients with juvenile idiopathic arthritis
pmc-11707685.creator: M. Huhtanen, K. Mikola, A. Kiukkonen, T. Palotie
pmc-11707685.description: ObjectiveTemporomandibular joint (TMJ) arthritis is a common finding in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) patients. TMJ arthritis can cause significant disturbances in TMJ function and growth without treatment. Our aim was to evaluate the effectiveness of medical treatments used to manage TMJ arthritis and how to evaluate the outcome of the treatment.

pmc-11864694.title: NLRP4 drives olaparib resistance in pancreatic cancer
pmc-11864694.creator: Mingming Xiao, Xianjun Yu, Si Shi
pmc-11864694.description: Olaparib has been approved as a treatment for metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in patients with BRCA1 (BRCA1 DNA repair associated) or BRCA2 mutations. However, a large portion of pancreatic cancer patients either exhibit inherent resistance or develop resistance over time. Understanding the molecular mechanisms that drive this resistance is crucial to develop more effective targeted therapies.

pmc-12396095.title: Conditioned plasma promotes full-thickness skin defect healing in a rat model
pmc-12396095.creator: Majid Zamani, Saeid Kaviani, Mehdi Yousefi, Saeid Abroun, Mohammad Hojjat-Farsangi, Behzad Pourabbas
pmc-12396095.description: IntroductionBlood derivatives may enhance wound healing, but each possesses distinct characteristics and has yielded varying outcomes in patient treatment. This research seeks to examine the efficacy of conditioned plasma (CP) using polylactic acid (PLA) coated beads and to compare it with CP using bare beads and platelet-rich plasma (PRP) in the context of acute wound healing.

pmc-12753834.title: ACPA prevents lung fibroblast-to-CAF transformation by reprogramming the tumor microenvironment through NSCLC-derived exosomes
pmc-12753834.creator: Özge Boyacıoğlu, Berfin Deniz Kalali, Tuba Reçber, Dilek Gelen-Gungor, Emirhan Nemutlu, İpek Eroğlu, Nedret Kılıç, Petek Korkusuz
pmc-12753834.description: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for most lung cancer cases. Current treatments often cause systemic side effects or lead to drug resistance, prompting the development of new therapies targeting tumors and related cells simultaneously. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are crucial stromal cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME), making them potential targets for therapy.

pmc-12785587.title: Beyond Leptin and Adiponectin: The Diverse Roles of Adipokines in the Myocardial Hypertrophic Process and Heart Failure and Their Potential Contribution in Obesity
pmc-12785587.creator: Morris Karmazyn, Xiaohong Tracey Gan
pmc-12785587.description: It is now widely recognized that adipocytes have the ability to produce a myriad of bioactive compounds released into the circulation and affecting distal organs, including the heart. These factors, termed adipokines, are also produced by various tissues in addition to adipocytes, including cardiac tissue, and have the ability to modulate cardiac function and the response to pathology.

pmc-13315006.title: A neural stem cell–derived 3D spheroid model that recapitulates prion infection and pathology
pmc-13315006.creator: Hyun Jung Park, Hyeri Kim, Sanghoon Byun, Chongsuk Ryou

pmc-13330634.title: Intraluminal Appendiceal Migration of an Intrauterine Device Without Appendicitis: A Case Report
pmc-13330634.creator: Ángel Sánchez Tinajero, Jusseline Villegas Amador, Dulce Diana Guerra Aguirre, Danna Patricia Ruiz Santillán, María del Carmen Zamora López, Anita Ríos Pérez, Juan Ramón Razo Blancas
pmc-13330634.description: Patient: Female, 37-year-old Final Diagnosis: Migrated intrauterine device (IUD) Symptoms: Abdominal pain Clinical Procedure: — Specialty: Obstetrics and Gynecology • Surgery Objective: Unusual clinical course BackgroundThe intrauterine device (IUD) is a commonly used contraceptive method in emerging countries, such as Mexico and several Latin American nations.

pmc-13575464.title: Emerging, personalized, and minimally invasive technologies for periodontal and peri‐implant soft and hard tissue regenerative therapy
pmc-13575464.creator: Shayan Barootchi, Lorenzo Tavelli, Hamoun Sabri, William V Giannobile, Darnell Kaigler
pmc-13575464.description: BackgroundRegenerative therapies have become central to periodontics and implant dentistry and are becoming more widely applied to reconstruct supporting bone and associated soft tissues. With increased recognition of the benefits of using biomimetic materials as scaffolds in contemporary regenerative technologies, the field is seeking to develop and optimize predictable, personalized regenerative strategies for hard and soft tissue reconstruction.

pmc-13613649.title: Screen time patterns and cognitive screening outcomes (MoCA-Ina) in adolescents: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13613649.creator: Pricilla Yani Gunawan, Andraina Andraina, Jeremiah Hilkiah Wijaya, Yang Yang Endro Arjuna, Patricia Yulita Gunawan
pmc-13613649.description: BackgroundAdolescent screen exposure is increasing, yet clinically interpretable thresholds for cognitive risk are unclear. This study examined associations between daily screen time and cognitive screening performance and derived a screen-time cutoff associated with cognitive impairment.MethodsWe conducted an observational cross-sectional study (March–April 2022) at a private junior high school in Indonesia during online learning.

pmc-13620166.title: Reinforcement-learning signals support dynamic adaptive control during language switching
pmc-13620166.creator: Mingyue Zuo, Huanhuan Liu, Linyan Liu, John W. Schwieter, Yan Jing Wu

pmc-13676684.title: Neurofilaments in cerebrospinal fluid and/or serum as a possible biomarker of pediatric spinal muscular atrophy
pmc-13676684.creator: Markéta Kumhera, Eva Vrsčaj, Tanja Loboda, Damjan Osredkar, Petra Holotová, Marie Rohlenová, Barbora Lauerová, Vanesa Jurášová, Jitka Hanzalová, Markéta Pavlíková, Jana Haberlová
pmc-13676684.description: BackgroundSpinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a severe, genetically determined neuromuscular disorder characterised by progressive muscle weakness resulting from motor neuron degeneration. Although therapies such as nusinersen have altered disease trajectories, objective biomarkers for treatment monitoring remain lacking. Neurofilament proteins, particularly phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNFH), are promising candidates for this role.
